title: Space in the day
tomorrow: three lines, each said three times. what do they actually promise?

cards: A calendar app will happily color in every hour of a Saturday, and some weeks it does.
Back in the bamboo park, Anuruddha has thought seven good thoughts: few wants, contentment, solitude, energy, mindfulness, stillness, wisdom. Every one is about walking the path well.
Then the Buddha adds the eighth, and it's strange. This teaching, he says, is for one who delights in nippapañca, not for one who delights in papañca.
Seven thoughts about doing it right, and the last word sounds like an instruction to stop. Why?

teach.b: Papañca is the mind spinning out: one thought making ten, a plan breeding another plan, a worry rehearsing itself until the hour is gone. Translators reach for proliferation, elaboration, sprawl.
Nippapañca is the un-spun: a mind with room in it. So here's the solve. The seven thoughts tell you what to do.

The eighth tells you what to stop filling. Without it, even the seven can turn into one more busy project: more effort, more mindfulness, more of everything, wound tighter. Another sutta comes at it from the other side.
Sariputta lists ways a monk lives that don't end well, and the list opens with delighting in busy work, then in talk, in sleep, in company, and it closes with delighting in papañca.
That's the one to tell a friend tonight: on a monk's list of warnings, busy work comes first.
So Buddhist life builds empty space in on purpose. The rains retreat keeps monks in one place for a season. On holy days some lay people set work aside for the precepts and a quiet day at the temple.
Space isn't laziness here. It's where the spinning slows down long enough for the mind to see.
Room to breathe is part of the path, not a break from it.

how: Buddhist life sets aside empty time on purpose: monks keep the rains retreat in one place, and on uposatha days some lay Buddhists put work aside to keep the precepts and spend a quiet day at the temple.

games.q: what does “space in the day” mean?
o: a lunch break scheduled between two meetings
a rest day earned by finishing all your work
an hour left empty so the mind can stop spinning

games.q: solve the eighth thought — tap the pairs.
p: the mind spinning one thought into ten
a mind with room in it
what to do on the path

s: the Buddha's eighth thought was about trying harder
it was about delighting in the un-spun mind: room, not more effort.
busy work is on Sariputta's list of ways a monk's life goes wrong
the list opens with delighting in busy work and closes with delighting in papañca.
in Buddhism, empty time is just laziness with a nicer name
the rains retreat and the holy days build space in on purpose, as part of the path.

games.q: your study group plans a full Saturday, color-coded, breaks timed to the minute. someone asks if you want to add one more session. what fits the eighth thought?
o: add it; more structure keeps the mind from wandering.
leave an hour unplanned, so the day has room to breathe.
cancel the whole plan; every plan is papañca.
games.why: the eighth thought isn't against plans; it's against the spin. a day with room in it lets the mind settle enough to see.

practice: Look at the next seven days and find one hour you could leave unplanned.

Ask what you hope that hour gives you, what usually rushes in to fill it, and one small thing that will guard it: a note, a closed laptop, a word to someone at home. Then rest in the empty space the sit gives you now.

wordCard.voice: Space in the day: an hour left un-spun, nippapañca you can actually put on a calendar.

orig.note: Pali: free of proliferation, the un-spun mind; the Buddha's eighth thought for Anuruddha.

carryVoice: For the road: room to breathe, left open on purpose. Forty-one of forty-five, nearly there.

sources.ref: Anguttara Nikaya 8.30 (Anuruddha Sutta: the eighth thought, delight in non-proliferation)
Anguttara Nikaya 6.14 (Bhaddaka Sutta: Sariputta on delight in work, talk, sleep, company, socializing and papañca)
